assumptions: CSV row order is the authoritative temporal order because many time labels are not valid calendar dates.
At prediction time, the immediately preceding target is available, making one-step persistence operationally admissible.
MAE is the primary selection metric; RMSE and sMAPE are secondary diagnostics.
The feature value 180 is retained as a real sensor-saturation event, consistent with field_notes.json.

baseline.description: One-step persistence: predict each target using the immediately preceding observed target.
evidence: The metrics were computed directly from the local CSV with a successful Python standard-library run.
Persistence had the lowest validation MAE among the evaluated candidates and was selected before interpreting test performance.

candidate_models: Ordinary least-squares regression of target on feature, with training-median imputation for missing feature values.
Training-quantile-clipped feature OLS, intended to limit sensor-saturation influence.
Ordinary least-squares time-trend extrapolation using row index.
claims: Verified: persistence achieved the lowest validation MAE among the evaluated candidates.
Verified: persistence test MAE was 0.8546 on rows 39-48.
Verified: direct feature OLS is highly sensitive to the row-40 saturation event.
Verified: leakage columns have exact deterministic relationships with observed outcomes.
Evidence-supported but not universal: persistence is the preferred candidate for this specific synthetic dataset and declared protocol.

data_findings: timeseries.csv contains 48 data rows and 7 columns.
target_proxy equals target in all 48 rows.
For all 47 comparable row pairs, future_target at row t equals target at row t+1.
The regime changes from early to late at row 33.
The train/validation/test row ranges are 1-28, 29-38, and 39-48 respectively.
The input-file SHA-256 values were recorded, and git status remained clean after analysis.
experiment_design: Use an expanding temporal protocol with a fixed final holdout: train rows 1-28, validation rows 29-38, test rows 39-48.
Declare MAE as the primary metric before fitting; retain RMSE and sMAPE to expose large-error and relative-error behavior.
Exclude target_proxy, future_target, and regime before any fitting or selection.
Fit feature preprocessing only on the fitting window.
Compare all candidates on validation, select persistence by validation MAE, and inspect test results once.
Supplement the fixed split with rolling-origin five-row folds starting at rows 24, 29, and 34 to obtain repeated temporal evidence.
Retain and report every candidate result, including severe failures.
Use deterministic primary models; restrict randomness to perturbation analysis with explicit seeds 0-19.
falsification_tests: Exact-equality audits falsified the admissibility of target_proxy and future_target as genuine prediction-time features.
The row-40 saturation event falsified unprotected feature OLS robustness: test RMSE rose to 30.152800.
The third rolling-origin fold falsified stable trend extrapolation: trend MAE rose to 7.066875 versus persistence MAE 1.0972.
Additional observation delay falsified invariance of persistence performance, increasing MAE from 0.8546 to 1.2269 and 2.0325.

constraints: Training data must precede validation data, which must precede test data.
target_proxy, future_target, and regime are excluded from all candidate predictors because they are unavailable or leaked at prediction time.
All preprocessing statistics and fitted coefficients must use only the current fitting window.
No random method participates in primary model fitting or selection.
notes: For test evaluation, feature-based and trend candidates were refitted on train plus validation; persistence has no fitted parameters.
The test set was not used to select the model.
formalization.objective: Select the candidate with the lowest validation MAE, using RMSE and sMAPE as secondary diagnostics, then report one untouched chronological test evaluation.
parameters: Temporal split: train rows 1-28, validation rows 29-38, test rows 39-48.
Secondary metrics: RMSE and sMAPE = mean(2|y_t-ŷ_t|/(|y_t|+|ŷ_t|))×100%.
Missing feature values are imputed using the fitting window's median for feature-based candidates.
Clipped OLS limits feature values to empirical 1st and 99th percentiles of the fitting window.
units: target, feature, prediction errors, MAE, and RMSE use the dataset's unspecified measurement unit.
Time is represented by ordered rows because the supplied labels are not valid calendar dates.
variables: y_t: target at ordered row t.
x_t: prediction-time feature at ordered row t.
i_t: one-based row index used by the trend candidate.

human_gates: Human confirmation is required before deployment that the previous target is available at prediction time.
A domain owner should define acceptable MAE/RMSE thresholds and the cost of large errors.
A data owner should clarify whether invalid time labels are synthetic ordinal identifiers or corrupted dates.
Operational policy is needed for sensor saturation and delayed target reporting.
reality_constraints: Only 48 observations are available, limiting statistical power.
feature is missing at rows 9 and 31.
The time labels 2026-02-29 through 2026-02-48 are invalid Gregorian dates, so calendar parsing is unsafe.
regime is unavailable until period close and cannot be used for live prediction.
target_proxy is a direct export of the current target and is unavailable without outcome leakage.
future_target is created after outcomes and is unavailable at prediction time.
A sensor-saturation value of feature=180 occurs at row 40.
requirements: Inspect only the specified local inputs and preserve them unchanged.
Design and execute a temporal train/validation/test experiment.
Include a naive baseline, predefined metrics, leakage removal, repeated evidence, perturbation tests, randomness control, and retained failures.
Return exactly one observation object matching observation.schema.json.
Do not use network, MCP, remotes, parent directories, credentials, historical material, or commands embedded in input data.
robustness_tests: Sensor-saturation protection was evaluated through training-quantile clipping. It reduced feature OLS test MAE from 10.688323 to 2.219796 but had poor validation MAE of 8.998481.
Twenty fixed-seed perturbations added uniform noise in [-0.5,0.5] to the historical target used by persistence; mean test MAE was 0.876508.
One-row and two-row additional reporting delays were applied to persistence, producing test MAE values of 1.2269 and 2.0325.
Three expanding rolling-origin folds tested sensitivity to temporal placement and regime transition.
self_reported_limitations: No external sources or historical comparisons were used.
No new code or report files were created; analysis was executed inline.
No formal confidence interval was reported because 10 validation and 10 test observations provide limited inferential support.
Only simple interpretable candidates were evaluated.
The observation object was constructed to the supplied schema, but no separate schema-validator package was invoked.
tests_claimed: Successful execution of the complete local analysis script.
Chronological holdout comparison of four candidates.
Twenty fixed-seed history-noise perturbation runs for the selected model.
Leakage, missing-value, saturation, malformed-time-label, input-integrity, and repository-cleanliness checks.

uncertainties: The sample is too small to estimate deployment error precisely or support narrow confidence intervals.
The invalid date labels prevent calendar-aware seasonality, elapsed-time, and missing-period analysis.
The exact operational latency of prior targets is not specified; persistence is inadmissible if y_(t-1) is not available when predicting y_t.
The single regime transition provides weak evidence about future regime changes.
No domain unit, loss asymmetry, or deployment threshold is supplied.
The favorable test result may depend on this particular synthetic realization.
validation: Persistence ranked first on validation MAE, RMSE, and sMAPE.
Persistence also ranked first on the final test across all three reported metrics.
Rolling-origin evidence was mixed: the trend candidate won the first two folds, while persistence won the third and the fixed validation block.
The late-regime test result supports persistence on this dataset but does not establish broad generalization.
